sections.heading: What Every El Paso Traffic Ticket Has in Common
paragraphs: A speeding ticket on I-10, a stop-sign ticket in the Lower Valley and a no-insurance citation on Montana Avenue look different, but legally they are the same animal: a Class C misdemeanor under the Texas Transportation Code, punishable by a fine of up to $200 for most violations plus court costs. There is no jail. What there is, in every case, is a conviction that the court reports to the Department of Public Safety if you pay the ticket — because paying is a guilty plea.

That conviction is what actually costs you. It sits on your driving record for three years, carries two points toward a license suspension (three if there was a crash), and your insurance carrier re-rates you at every renewal. The $200 fine is the small part. The other thing every ticket has in common is that it is negotiable, and Robert Navar has spent more than ten years on these dockets.

sections.heading: The Three Outcomes We Work For on Every Citation
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance the same business day. From then on the court communicates with our office, and no failure-to-appear warrant can issue for a missed date. Then we pull the citation and look for leverage.

On the pretrial docket we negotiate for one of three results. The best is an outright dismissal — nothing reported, nothing on your record. The most common is deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45.051: you pay a court fee, stay violation-free for 90 to 180 days, and the case is dismissed without a conviction. Where a judge won't defer — high speeds, some school-zone cases, drivers who used deferral in the last year — we work for a reduction to a non-moving violation that insurers don't rate.

sections.heading: Flat Fees by Court: $59 Municipal, $69 Everywhere Else
paragraphs: Our pricing is set by the court your ticket is in, not by the charge. Citations written by the El Paso Police Department go to El Paso Municipal Court and cost a flat $59 per ticket. Citations from the Sheriff, a constable or a DPS trooper go to one of the Justice of the Peace precincts, and tickets from the smaller cities go to Horizon City, Socorro, or the San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton municipal courts — all $69.

Additional citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons of $10 to $30 shown at checkout. The consultation is free, and an existing warrant is $35 for the first and $20 for each additional. sections.heading: How to Pick the Right Ticket Page
paragraphs: Start with the words on the citation. The most common is a plain speeding ticket; if the stop was in a flashing-light zone near a campus, see school zone speeding, which many judges treat more strictly. Ran a light at Mesa and Sunland Park, or rolled a stop in a neighborhood? That's the red light and stop sign ticket page. A phone in your hand on Loop 375 is a texting and cell phone ticket under Transportation Code 545.4251.

Paperwork tickets have their own fixes. No insurance (FMFR) carries a higher fine range but is often dismissed with proof of coverage; expired registration and inspection tickets usually go away once you renew. If you were stopped without a license, the distinction matters: no driver's license means you never had one or didn't have it with you, while driving while license invalid (DWLI) means it was suspended — and DWLI can climb to a Class B with a prior.

Professional drivers should go straight to the CDL ticket page, because federal rules bar most deferrals for commercial license holders, or to trucking and DOT violations for logbook, weight and equipment citations. If a trooper wrote the ticket on I-10 or US-54, see DPS state trooper tickets — those go to JP court, not Municipal. And for anything that isn't a moving violation at all — a loose-dog citation, a noise ordinance, a city code case — the Class C misdemeanors and city ordinance page covers it.
This page is general information, not legal advice about your case. If none of the categories fit, call 915-503-1600; se habla español, and the consultation is free.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to court if I hire you for a traffic ticket in El Paso?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. We file an appearance and handle the pretrial docket for you. You would only appear if the case went to trial, which is rare for a Class C ticket.

faqs.q: How much does a traffic ticket lawyer cost in El Paso?
faqs.a: A flat $59 per ticket in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 in Justice of the Peace, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts. Extra citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons, and the consultation is free. You can hire online and pay at checkout.

faqs.q: Is it better to just pay the ticket?
faqs.a: Paying is a guilty plea and a conviction on your record for three years. Compared with the insurance increase that usually follows, the $59–$69 fee is the cheaper path in nearly every case, and the most common result is no conviction at all.

faqs.q: What if my court date already passed?
faqs.a: There is probably a warrant and a separate failure-to-appear charge, but it is fixable. See our warrants hub or call us the same day; we can usually have a traffic warrant recalled within a day or two and reset the case.
